title: all_transactions has no production caller and drops earlier pages' evidence
body:
## Summary
`Client::all_transactions` (crates/table-paypal/src/secondary.rs:237) is pub and advertised in STATUS, but only tests call it, and when page N fails it returns that page's error alone, so the observations from pages 1 to N-1 are lost.

## Description
A workspace grep finds its only callers in crates/table-paypal/tests/client.rs:334,370,373. Reconciliation reads `transactions` page by page itself, and crates/table-app/src/pipeline/resolve.rs:820 keeps the observations across pages. Inside all_transactions, `self.transactions(window).await?` (crates/table-paypal/src/secondary.rs:250) returns the later page's error, and the earlier pages' `observations` vector is lost. This round fixed the same kind of defect in the token refresh. The fix is one of two: delete the method together with the STATUS line that advertises it (docs/build/STATUS.md:588), or keep it and merge the earlier observations into the error.

## Flow
- page 1 answers 200 (total_pages 2), page 2 transport-fails
- `?` returns Error::Unknown with page 2's single status-0 observation
- page 1's 200 observation is gone

## Expected impact
Nobody is affected today because nothing at runtime calls it. The risk is that its first real caller gets incomplete evidence. Deleting it breaks nothing outside the tests.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one pagination path, no lost evidence
Before: 0 production callers (grep); 1 of 2 observations returned on a page-2 failure (walked)
After: deleted: 0 dead pub items; or fixed: 2 of 2 observations
Method: simulation - walked the two-page case; whether to delete or keep is the operator's product call on reporting
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
grep -rn all_transactions crates -> only crates/table-paypal/src/secondary.rs:237 and crates/table-paypal/tests/client.rs:334,370,373
crates/table-paypal/src/secondary.rs:250  let response = self.transactions(window).await?;
instrument: test: page(1) ok then Err(TransportError) -> error.observations().len()==2 (red today); or delete it and keep cargo test -p table-paypal -p table-app green

title: Retry a transient OAuth token failure like the API call it guards
body:
## Summary
The token request (crates/table-paypal/src/client.rs:93-146) is never retried, but the API call after it is retried on transport errors, 429 and 5xx. A single transient 503 from the token endpoint therefore fails the money call immediately.

## Description
execute_policy retries transport failures and 429/5xx (crates/table-paypal/src/client.rs:196-246) up to ATTEMPTS=3 with backoff. `token()` turns every failure into Error::Credentials (client.rs:116,118,126,134), and execute_policy returns that on attempt 0. Nothing has been sent at that point, so retrying the token request is safe. A `credentials.load()` failure (empty keychain) must NOT be retried, because waiting 3 s cannot fix it. So token() first has to tell a load failure apart from a token-endpoint failure. The rule: retry only token-endpoint transport errors and 5xx/429, inside the same attempt budget.

## Flow
- token endpoint answers 503 once
- token() -> Error::Credentials
- execute_policy returns before any API request; the owner's action fails as 'credentials unavailable'

## Expected impact
Owner-approved captures and voids fail less often during short PayPal outages. Possible cost: up to 3 s of extra latency when the token endpoint is fully down.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a transient token failure no longer fails the call
Before: [oauth 503, oauth 200, api 200] -> Err(Credentials) after 1 token request (walked from code)
After: Ok after 2 token requests; an empty keychain still fails with 1 load and 0 waits
Method: simulation - walked the code; the test is about 20 lines, but the fix has to split token()'s error and is a behaviour choice, so it goes to A/B
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: test in crates/table-paypal/tests/client.rs: setup([response(503,{}), oauth(), response(200, order_wire)]) -> get_order Ok with 2 /token requests; plus a failing Credentials impl -> 0 backoff waits

title: One PayPal call can hold the pipeline for about two and a half minutes
body:
## Summary
No overall deadline limits a PayPal call. The worst case is token 30 s + 3 attempts x 30 s + backoff 1+2 s = 123 s, or 153 s when a 401 forces a token refresh, and the pipeline is borrowed `&mut` the whole time.

## Description
REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS=30 (crates/table-paypal/src/http.rs:75) limits one request, and ATTEMPTS=3 (crates/table-paypal/src/client.rs:10) plus backoff_secs (http.rs:77) multiply it. No tokio::time::timeout wraps execute_policy or the Pipeline call sites (grep finds none in crates/table-app/src). Pipeline methods take `&mut self` (e.g. crates/table-app/src/pipeline.rs:186, tick at :626), so every other deal's deadline default waits behind one slow call. The fix: a per-call deadline (e.g. 45 s); when it passes, the outcome is Unknown and carries the observations made so far.

## Flow
- PayPal accepts the TCP connection and stalls each request
- each attempt times out at 30 s; two backoffs
- the call returns Unknown after ~123 s, and tick() runs the other deals' deadlines that much late

## Expected impact
Deadline defaults (void on expiry) still run on time while PayPal stalls. Risk: a deadline that is too short turns slow successes into Unknowns that then need reconciliation.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - bounded wall time per PayPal call
Before: 123 s worst case (153 s with a 401 refresh), computed from the constants
After: <= the chosen deadline (e.g. 45 s), measured under tokio paused time
Method: simulation - arithmetic over the constants; the instrument is a paused-clock test with a stalling transport
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: #[tokio::test(start_paused = true)] with a Transport that sleeps REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS then errors: assert elapsed <= deadline and that Error::Unknown carries 1 or more observations

title: Error::Credentials hides which of five failures happened
body:
## Summary
Five different failures become the same Error::Credentials ('credentials unavailable'): the keychain load fails, the token request fails in transport, the token endpoint answers non-200, access_token is missing, or expires_in is bad. An offline wallet and a revoked app therefore show the same error.

## Description
crates/table-paypal/src/client.rs:116,118,126,134 and the Credentials implementation (crates/table-runtime/src/vault.rs:139-142) all return the unit variant Error::Credentials (crates/table-paypal/src/types.rs:251). The operator cannot tell 'network down' from 'PayPal rejected the app secret' from 'keychain empty', and nothing records which one happened. The fix: give the variant a reason, e.g. Credentials { kind: Missing|Rejected|Unreachable|Malformed }, with no secret in it, and show it in the audit detail. Changing the pub enum touches table-runtime, which is outside this round's paths.

## Flow
- network off; an owner approves a capture
- token request transport-fails -> Error::Credentials
- the wallet says credentials are unavailable, and the owner re-enters a secret that was fine

## Expected impact
The owner and the operator see the real cause. What could break: every match on Error::Credentials (vault.rs builds it; grep finds no match in table-app).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a failure names its cause
Before: 5 causes -> 1 variant that cannot tell them apart (counted)
After: 5 causes -> 4 distinguishable kinds, none carrying a secret
Method: simulation - counted the sites; the change crosses into table-runtime
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: test: transport Err on /token -> kind Unreachable; 401 on /token -> Rejected; assert Display contains no id/secret

title: Pin the transport's no-redirect and 1 MiB cap with a loopback test
body:
## Summary
ReqwestTransport has two safety properties and no test for either: it never follows a redirect (so the Bearer header never goes to another host), and it fails any answer over 1 MiB.

## Description
crates/table-paypal/src/http.rs:101 sets redirect::Policy::none(), and http.rs:145 caps the body at 1_048_576 bytes. The only http.rs tests cover header_pair (http.rs:171-194), so removing either line leaves `cargo test -p table-paypal` green. A test against a 127.0.0.1 listener needs no network (tests/spikes.rs:194 already binds one). AGENTS.md says tests never touch the network, and whether a loopback socket counts is the reviewer's call, so this goes to Lane B.

## Flow
- loopback server answers 302 Location: http://127.0.0.1:<other>/
- ReqwestTransport.send returns status 302 and the second listener sees no request
- loopback server streams 1 MiB + 1 bytes -> TransportError

## Expected impact
A future change to reqwest's defaults, or a refactor that drops either line, turns the test red. Risk: a flaky socket test on CI.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - two security properties pinned
Before: 0 of 2 properties caught by a mutant (from reading: no test builds ReqwestTransport offline)
After: 2 of 2
Method: simulation - the test itself is what this card delivers; not built here because of the loopback-vs-network rule
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: loopback test in the crates/table-paypal/src/http.rs tests: change Policy::none() to the default and the cap to usize::MAX; each must go red

title: zeroize and time are pinned per crate, outside the workspace table
body:
## Summary
`zeroize = "1"` is declared separately in 6 manifests and `time = {version="0.3",features=[...]}` in 2. Every other dependency that table-paypal shares with other crates comes from [workspace.dependencies].

## Description
crates/table-paypal/Cargo.toml:13 (time) and :24 (zeroize). The same zeroize line appears in table-engine, table-mcp, table-os, table-runtime and services/house-seller, and the same time line in table-ledger. The workspace root Cargo.toml declares neither. A version bump or feature change has to be made in 8 places, and AGENTS.md asks for few, mainstream, justified dependencies. The fix: two [workspace.dependencies] rows and `.workspace = true` in the 8 manifests. The root manifest is outside this round's paths.

## Flow
- grep for zeroize and time in crates/*/Cargo.toml and services/*/Cargo.toml
- 8 per-crate pins, 0 workspace rows

## Expected impact
Each dependency is bumped in one place. Nothing should break, because the versions and features are already identical.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one declaration per shared dependency
Before: 8 per-crate declarations (counted)
After: 2 workspace rows and 8 inherits; cargo tree -d unchanged
Method: probe - counted on the tree; the change is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: cargo metadata before/after shows identical resolved versions; cargo check --workspace exit 0

title: Concurrent 401s clear a freshly refreshed token
body:
## Summary
On a 401, execute_policy clears the cached token (crates/table-paypal/src/client.rs:239) without checking that it is the token the failed request used.

## Description
With concurrent callers, a second 401 could throw away a token another call had just fetched. But the only runtime holder, Pipeline, calls the API through `&mut self` (crates/table-app/src/pipeline.rs:186), so calls never overlap.

## Flow
- two concurrent calls - cannot happen through Pipeline

## Expected impact
None.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer token requests
Before: 0 concurrent callers -> 0 extra token requests
After: 0 extra token requests
Method: probe - read every holder of the PayPalApi
Result: not-better
Gate: none
